locations.name: Hobbiton
locations.description: A hobbit village in the heart of the Shire, where Bag End stood.
locations.explanation: Hobbiton lay in the central part of the Shire, in the Westfarthing, on both sides of the Water and about a mile north-west of Bywater.

references.supports: A village in the central regions of the Shire, within the Westfarthing; on both sides of the Water, about a mile north-west of Bywater.

locations.name: Bree
locations.description: A village of Men and hobbits at the crossing of two great roads.
locations.explanation: Bree lay just east of the crossing of the East Road and the Greenway, about forty miles east of the Shire, east of the Old Forest and the Barrow-downs, west of Weathertop and south of Fornost.

references.supports: Village east of the crossing of the East Road and the Greenway; Bree-land about forty miles east of the Shire, east of the Old Forest and Barrow-downs, west of Weathertop, south of Fornost Erain.

locations.name: Weathertop
locations.description: A hill topped by the ruins of an ancient watchtower, also called Amon Sûl.
locations.explanation: Weathertop (Amon Sûl) was the southernmost top of the Weather Hills, which lay at the centre of Arnor near the East Road, east of Bree.

references.supports: Southernmost top of the Weather Hills; the Weather Hills lay at the centre of Arnor, near the East Road.
Bree-land lay west of Weathertop.

locations.name: Rivendell
locations.description: Elrond's hidden refuge, the Last Homely House.
locations.explanation: Rivendell (Imladris) lay on the eastern edge of Eriador, in the foothills of the Misty Mountains, at the edge of a narrow gorge of the river Bruinen.

references.supports: An Elven outpost in the Misty Mountains on the eastern edge of Eriador; at the edge of a narrow gorge of the Bruinen, hidden in the moorlands and foothills of the Misty Mountains.

locations.name: Moria
locations.description: The vast Dwarf-realm beneath the Misty Mountains, also called Khazad-dûm.
locations.explanation: Moria lay in the central parts of the Misty Mountains, tunnelled through them from the West-gate to the East-gate, which opened on Dimrill Dale on the eastern side of the range.

references.supports: Lay in the central parts of the Misty Mountains and traversed them from east to west; West-gate and East-gate at least forty miles apart.
Dimrill Dale was a valley on the east side of the Misty Mountains, at the eastern end of the Redhorn Pass.

locations.name: Lothlórien
locations.description: The golden Elven wood of the Galadhrim, with the only mallorn-trees east of the Sea.
locations.explanation: Lothlórien was the forest between the Misty Mountains and the Great River Anduin, below the Gladden; its city, Caras Galadhon, stood in the angle between the rivers Celebrant and Anduin.

references.supports: The forest between the mountains and the Great River, above the Limlight and below the Gladden; the only mallorn-trees east of the sea.
Caras Galadhon was in the angle between the rivers Celebrant and Anduin.

locations.name: Isengard
locations.description: Saruman's fortress, ringed by a wall of stone around the tower of Orthanc.
locations.explanation: Isengard (Angrenost) lay in a valley at the southern tip of the Misty Mountains, near the Gap of Rohan.

references.supports: A fortress in a valley at the southern end of the Misty Mountains near the Gap of Rohan; domain of Saruman.

locations.name: Helm's Deep
locations.description: A great gorge and fortress, a refuge of the Rohirrim.
locations.explanation: Helm's Deep was a gorge below the Thrihyrne, at the head of the Westfold Vale near the end of the northernmost arm of the White Mountains, about fifteen miles from the Fords of Isen.

references.supports: A gorge below the Thrihyrne at the head of the Westfold Vale, near the end of the northernmost arm of the White Mountains; about five leagues (15 miles) from the mouth of the Deeping-coomb to the Fords of Isen.

locations.name: Edoras
locations.description: The capital of Rohan, home of the golden hall Meduseld.
locations.explanation: Edoras was built on a hill in Harrowdale, a valley of the White Mountains under the Starkhorn; the river Snowbourn flowed past it on its way west to the Entwash.

references.supports: Capital of Rohan with the Golden Hall of Meduseld; on a hill in Harrowdale, under the Starkhorn; the Snowbourn flowed past it west toward the Entwash.
Edoras lay on the slopes of the White Mountains.

locations.name: Minas Tirith
locations.description: The White City, capital of Gondor, once called Minas Anor.
locations.explanation: Minas Tirith (Minas Anor) lay south-west of Osgiliath, which stood about halfway between it and Minas Ithil; Cair Andros lay about fifty miles to its north.

references.supports: Minas Anor; capital of the South-kingdom from T.A. 1640.
Osgiliath lay about halfway between Minas Anor to the south-west and Minas Ithil to the north-east.
Cair Andros lay about fifty miles north of Minas Tirith.

locations.name: Pelargir
locations.description: The great harbour city of Gondor on the Anduin.
locations.explanation: Pelargir was a great city on the river Anduin and the main harbour of Gondor; the coast of the Bay of Belfalas retreated after the Downfall of Númenor, leaving it far inland.

references.supports: A great city on the Anduin and the main harbour of Gondor; left far inland by the retreat of the coast along the Bay of Belfalas.

locations.name: The Black Gate
locations.description: The Morannon, the main entrance into the land of Mordor.
locations.explanation: The Black Gate (Morannon) closed the pass of Cirith Gorgor, between the Ephel Dúath and the Ered Lithui, in the north-western corner of Mordor; the plain of the Dagorlad lay north of it.

references.supports: The main entrance into Mordor; blocked the pass of Cirith Gorgor between the Ephel Dúath and the Ered Lithui in the north-western corner of Mordor; the Dagorlad lay further north.

locations.name: Mount Doom
locations.description: The volcano Orodruin, where the One Ring was forged and where it was unmade.
locations.explanation: Mount Doom (Orodruin) stood alone on the Plateau of Gorgoroth in Mordor, about thirty miles west of Barad-dûr.

references.supports: A volcano in Mordor that stood alone in the Plateau of Gorgoroth, connected to the Dark Tower by Sauron's Road.
Barad-dûr stood about 30 miles east of Mount Doom.

locations.name: Erebor
locations.description: The Lonely Mountain, the Dwarf-kingdom where the dragon Smaug dwelt.
locations.explanation: Erebor, the Lonely Mountain, stood alone in the north-east of Rhovanion and was the source of the river Running; the valley of Dale lay at its southern foot.

references.supports: A large, solitary mountain in the north-east of Rhovanion and the source of the river Running.
The valley of Dale lay between the south-western and south-eastern arms of the Lonely Mountain.
Smaug dwelt in the Lonely Mountain.

locations.name: The Grey Havens
locations.description: The Elven seaport from which ships sail into the West.
locations.explanation: The Grey Havens (Mithlond) were seaports on both sides of the end of the Gulf of Lune, near the mouth of the river Lhûn, in the far west of Eriador.

references.supports: Seaports on both sides of the end of the Gulf of Lune near the mouth of the Lhûn in western Eriador; ships sailed West from them.

locations.name: Amon Hen
locations.description: The Hill of Sight, crowned by the ruined Seat of Seeing.
locations.explanation: Amon Hen rose beside the Anduin near Tol Brandir, with the lawn of Parth Galen at its eastern foot; the Fellowship broke up near the southern edge of the Emyn Muil.

references.supports: On its eastern side at the foot lay the lawn of Parth Galen and the Anduin that flowed past Tol Brandir; the Seat of Seeing was on the summit.
The Fellowship broke up near the southern boundary of the Emyn Muil.

locations.name: Fangorn Forest
locations.description: The deep, dark forest of the Ents, where Treebeard lives.
locations.explanation: Fangorn Forest grew on the eastern flank of the southern Misty Mountains, north of Rohan, where it was known as the Entwood; the river Entwash flowed through it.

references.supports: A deep woodland beneath the southern Misty Mountains, on the eastern side of the range; known as the Entwood in Rohan; the Entwash flowed through it.
A large forest to the north of Rohan where Treebeard and the other Ents live.

locations.name: The Dead Marshes
locations.description: Reeking wetlands that Gollum guided Frodo and Sam across.
locations.explanation: The Dead Marshes lay north-west of the Dagorlad and south-east of the Emyn Muil, on the road from the hills toward the Black Gate.

references.supports: Reeking wetlands north-west of the Dagorlad and south-east of the Emyn Muil; Gollum revealed a hidden way across them after meeting Frodo and Sam in the Emyn Muil.

locations.name: Minas Morgul
locations.description: A pale, fell city that was once Gondor's Minas Ithil, the Tower of the Moon.
locations.explanation: Minas Morgul stood within the narrow Morgul Vale, guarding the pass between Ithilien and Mordor; the Morgul-road ran to it from Osgiliath, which lay to the south-west.

references.supports: Situated within the narrow Morgul Vale, guarding the pass between Ithilien and Mordor; the Morgul-road ran from Osgiliath.
Osgiliath lay about halfway between Minas Anor to the south-west and Minas Ithil to the north-east; Minas Ithil was taken in 2002.

locations.name: Osgiliath
locations.description: The ruined old capital of Gondor, divided by a great river.
locations.explanation: Osgiliath stood on both sides of the Anduin, about halfway between Minas Anor to the south-west and Minas Ithil to the north-east, north of the Emyn Arnen.

references.supports: Stood on both sides of the Anduin, about halfway between Minas Anor (south-west) and Minas Ithil (north-east), north of Emyn Arnen.

locations.name: Cirith Ungol
locations.description: A high, difficult pass into Mordor, watched by a tower and a giant spider.
locations.explanation: Cirith Ungol was a pass through the Ephel Dúath into Mordor, in a cleft on the north-east side of the Morgul Vale, above and north of the Morgul Pass.

references.supports: A pass through the Ephel Dúath into Mordor, in a cleft on the north-east side of the Morgul Vale, above and north of the Morgul Pass.
Cirith Ungol was a higher, more difficult pass guarded by Shelob and the Tower of Cirith Ungol.

locations.name: Barad-dûr
locations.description: Sauron's Dark Tower, his main fortress.
locations.explanation: Barad-dûr stood on a spur of the Ered Lithui in the northern part of the Plateau of Gorgoroth, about thirty miles east of Mount Doom and about a hundred miles south-east of the Black Gate.

references.supports: Built on the end of a long south-western spur of the Ered Lithui in the northern part of the Plateau of Gorgoroth; about 30 miles east of Mount Doom and about 100 miles south-east of the Black Gate.

locations.name: Dol Guldur
locations.description: The hill-fortress where the Necromancer hid, once called Amon Lanc.
locations.explanation: Dol Guldur stood at the highest point of a highland in the south-west of Mirkwood, east of the Anduin and facing Lothlórien across the river.

references.supports: A stronghold of Sauron at the highest point of a highland in the south-west of Mirkwood; originally Amon Lanc; Lothlórien lay to the west.
Mirkwood was a great forest east of the Anduin; Amon Lanc lay south and west of the Narrows of the Forest.

locations.name: Dale
locations.description: The town of Men that grew up in the shadow of the Lonely Mountain.
locations.explanation: Dale lay in a valley between the south-western and south-eastern arms of the Lonely Mountain, within a loop of the river Running, which flowed on south to the Long Lake.

references.supports: The valley lay between the south-western and south-eastern arms of the Lonely Mountain; the town was near its southern end within a loop of the river, which flowed south to the Long Lake.

locations.name: Lake-town
locations.description: A wooden town built on pillars in a lake, also called Esgaroth.
locations.explanation: Lake-town stood on the west side of the Long Lake, a little north of the mouth of the Forest River, in a calm bay sheltered by a rock promontory. After Smaug's fall it was rebuilt a little to the north.

references.supports: On the west side of the lake, a bit north of the mouth of the Forest River in a calm bay sheltered by a rock promontory; rebuilt to the north of its original location.

locations.name: Dunharrow
locations.description: A mountain refuge of the Rohirrim beside the entrance to the Paths of the Dead.
locations.explanation: Dunharrow was a fortified refuge in the White Mountains south of Edoras, with the Írensaga to the north, the Starkhorn to the south and the Dwimorberg to the east.

references.supports: A fortified refuge of the Rohirrim in the White Mountains south of Edoras, between the Írensaga (north), the Starkhorn (south) and the Dwimorberg (east); the entrance to the Paths of the Dead lay below the Dwimorberg.

locations.name: The Barrow-downs
locations.description: Treeless hills crowned with ancient burial mounds.
locations.explanation: The Barrow-downs were treeless hills east of the Shire, behind the Old Forest, and south-west of the village of Bree.

references.supports: A series of treeless hills east of the Shire, behind the Old Forest, and south-west of Bree.

locations.name: Dol Amroth
locations.description: The seat of a princedom, on a headland above the sea.
locations.explanation: Dol Amroth was a stronghold on a promontory and peninsula in Gondor facing the Bay of Belfalas, seat of a hereditary princedom.

references.supports: A promontory ruled as a hereditary princedom from its stronghold on a peninsula in Gondor facing the Bay of Belfalas.

locations.name: Emyn Muil
locations.description: A maze of difficult rocky hills where Frodo and Sam met Gollum.
locations.explanation: The Emyn Muil were hills around the lake Nen Hithoel, north of the falls of Rauros, south of the Brown Lands and north of the Nindalf; the Anduin ran through them.

references.supports: A range of hills around the lake Nen Hithoel, north of the falls of Rauros; south of the Brown Lands and north of the Nindalf; the Anduin flowed through the hills.

locations.name: The Iron Hills
locations.description: A range of hills rich in iron and home to a Dwarf-realm.
locations.explanation: The Iron Hills were a range in the north-east of Wilderland, east of the Lonely Mountain; an old road ran east to them from Dale.

references.supports: A range of great hills in the north-east of Wilderland, rich in iron and home to a Dwarf-realm.
An old road led from the valley of Dale to the east towards the Iron Hills.

locations.name: Fornost
locations.period: Third Age: capital of Arthedain until it was captured in T.A. 1974
locations.description: The second capital of Arnor and later the capital of Arthedain.
locations.explanation: Fornost Erain stood at the south end of the North Downs, about a hundred miles north of Bree, at the northern end of the North-South Road.

references.supports: Located at the south end of the North Downs, about 100 miles north of Bree, at the northern end of the North-South Road; captured by Angmar in T.A. 1974.

locations.name: Carn Dûm
locations.period: Third Age: seat of the king of Angmar until the realm fell in T.A. 1975
locations.description: The chief fortress of Angmar and seat of its king.
locations.explanation: Carn Dûm stood at the north-western end of the Mountains of Angmar, the north-western extension of the Misty Mountains.

references.supports: The chief fortress of Angmar and the seat of its king, at the north-western end of the Mountains of Angmar.
The Misty Mountains continued past Mount Gundabad in a north-westerly direction as the Mountains of Angmar; Angmar was destroyed in 1975.

locations.name: Annúminas
locations.period: Third Age: an early capital of Arnor, later ruined
locations.description: The city of the Kings of Arnor before the capital moved to Fornost.
locations.explanation: Annúminas lay on the south-east shore of Lake Nenuial (Evendim), near the source of the river Baranduin, with the Hills of Evendim to its south and west.

references.supports: On the south-east shore of Lake Nenuial, near the source of the Baranduin; the Hills of Evendim rose to the south and west; the capital later moved to Fornost Erain.

locations.name: Tharbad
locations.period: Third Age: ruined and deserted after floods in T.A. 2912
locations.description: A ford and fortified town where the North-South Road crossed a great river.
locations.explanation: Tharbad stood on the southern border of Eriador, a few miles downstream from where the Hoarwell and the Glanduin join to form the Gwathló, which the North-South Road crossed there.

references.supports: On the southern border of Eriador, a few miles downstream from the confluence of the Hoarwell and the Glanduin; the North-South Road crossed the Gwathló there; ruined and deserted in T.A. 2912.

locations.name: Ost-in-Edhil
locations.period: Second Age: capital of Eregion until its fall in S.A. 1697
locations.description: The Elven capital of Eregion, where Celebrimbor ruled.
locations.explanation: Ost-in-Edhil was the capital of Eregion (Hollin), west of the Misty Mountains and near the West-gate of Moria, joined to it by a highroad. Its exact site is not fixed; this map places it west of Moria.

references.supports: Eregion lay in Eriador west of the Misty Mountains near the West-gate of Moria; Ost-in-Edhil was its capital; a high road ran from Ost-in-Edhil to Khazad-dûm.
The highroad connected Ost-in-Edhil with the west gate of Moria; its exact location is uncertain, possibly near the Sirannon many miles downstream from the West-gate.
Elrond founded Rivendell in S.A. 1697 after the Fall of Eregion.

locations.name: Mount Gundabad
locations.description: A northern mountain revered by Dwarves but usually held by Orcs.
locations.explanation: Mount Gundabad stood beside the northern end of the Misty Mountains, where they met the Grey Mountains to the east and the Mountains of Angmar to the north-west.

references.supports: Appeared as the northern endpoint of the Misty Mountains and the western endpoint of the Grey Mountains; the Misty Mountains continued past it north-westwards as the Mountains of Angmar; usually occupied by Orcs.
In the far north the Misty Mountains met the Grey Mountains and the Mountains of Angmar, forming a T; Gundabad is the northernmost peak.

locations.name: Dimrill Dale
locations.description: The valley below the East-gate of Moria, source of the Silverlode, with the lake Mirrormere.
locations.explanation: Dimrill Dale was a valley on the east side of the Misty Mountains, beneath the Redhorn, Silvertine and Cloudyhead; the Silverlode rose there and the Mirrormere lay at its south-east corner.

references.supports: A valley on the east side of the Misty Mountains beneath the Redhorn, Silvertine and Cloudyhead; source of the Silverlode, with the Mirrormere at its south-east corner.
The Battle of Nanduhirion was fought in the valley beneath Moria's East-gate.

locations.name: Beorn's Hall
locations.description: The wooden house of Beorn, with its bee-hives and great garden.
locations.explanation: Beorn's Hall lay near the Carrock, east of the Great River of Wilderland and just west of Mirkwood.

references.supports: The Hall lay near the Carrock, east of the Great River of Wilderland, just west of Mirkwood.

locations.name: The Fords of Isen
locations.description: The crossings of the river Isen, the main western entrance to Rohan.
locations.explanation: The Fords of Isen lay a few miles north of the point where the Isen turns west towards the sea in the Gap of Rohan, south of Isengard, where the Misty Mountains and the White Mountains draw close.

references.supports: A few miles north of where the Isen turned west toward the sea in the Gap of Rohan; the only place the river could be crossed south of Isengard; the main entrance to Rohan from Eriador.

locations.name: Cair Andros
locations.description: A long river-island in the Anduin, shaped like a ship.
locations.explanation: Cair Andros was a river-island in the Anduin a little over ten miles long, east of Anórien and about fifty miles north of Minas Tirith.

references.supports: A long, narrow river-island in the Anduin, a little over ten miles long, east of Anórien and about fifty miles north of Minas Tirith.

locations.name: The Isenmouthe
locations.description: Carach Angren, the fenced iron pass in the north-west of Mordor.
locations.explanation: The Isenmouthe (Carach Angren) was a pass in the north-west of Mordor, where spurs of the Ephel Dúath and the Ered Lithui met, leaving a narrow way between the Plateau of Gorgoroth and the valley of Udûn to the north.

references.supports: A pass in the north-west of Mordor formed where spurs of the Ephel Dúath and the Ered Lithui met, leaving a narrow passage between the Plateau of Gorgoroth and the valley of Udûn to the north.

locations.name: Umbar
locations.description: The great haven of the Corsairs on the coast south of Gondor.
locations.explanation: Umbar lay on the coast south of Gondor, south of the mouth of the Anduin on the Bay of Belfalas, in a natural haven formed by a peninsula.

references.supports: A realm on the coast south of Gondor, south of the mouth of the Anduin at the Bay of Belfalas, in a natural haven formed by a peninsula.

locations.name: Edhellond
locations.period: Third Age: an ancient harbour, founded in the late First Age
locations.description: An ancient Elven harbour in southern Gondor.
locations.explanation: Edhellond lay in southern Gondor, south-west of where the Ringló joins the Morthond, near the point where their waters flowed into Cobas Haven.

references.supports: An ancient harbour in southern Gondor, south-west of where the Ringló entered the Morthond, near where the combined waters flowed into Cobas Haven; many of the Galadhrim sailed from it in T.A. 1980.

locations.name: Henneth Annûn
locations.description: Faramir's hidden refuge behind a curtain of water.
locations.explanation: Henneth Annûn was a hidden Gondorian outpost north-east of Cair Andros in North Ithilien, a cave behind a west-facing waterfall.

references.supports: A hidden Gondorian outpost north-east of Cair Andros in North Ithilien; a cave behind a west-facing waterfall.

locations.name: The Old Forest
locations.description: A small, hostile forest, home of Old Man Willow.
locations.explanation: The Old Forest lay east of the Shire, bordered by the Brandywine on the west and the Barrow-downs on the east; the Withywindle ran roughly through its centre.

references.supports: A small forested area east of the Shire, bordered by the Barrow-downs in the east and the Brandywine in the west; the Withywindle lay roughly in its centre.
